summary: Return typed errors, cover both failure variants in an integration test, and run the suite with all features.

scenario.briefing: The quantity parser hides every failure behind a default zero, and the test suite only checks the happy path. Return typed errors, cover both variants, and run the suite with every feature.

misconceptions.description: Returning a default value instead of the parse error.
misconceptions.testDescription: Non-numeric input becomes a typed parse error.
misconceptions.feedback: unwrap_or(0) erases the failure and reports a successful zero. Use map_err to preserve the typed error.

misconceptions.description: Treating zero as a valid parsed quantity.
misconceptions.testDescription: Zero is rejected with its own error.
misconceptions.feedback: The parse succeeds for 0, so the domain check has to reject it explicitly with QuantityError::Zero.
A test suite that only proves success cannot catch a swallowed error. Assert NotANumber and Zero.

misconceptions.description: Assuming cargo test compiles feature-gated tests.
misconceptions.feedback: A cfg-gated test module is not compiled unless the feature is enabled. Use cargo test --all-features or a feature matrix.

sections.title: Errors are part of the API
sections.body: A Result<u32, QuantityError> tells the caller that parsing can fail and which failures are possible. Returning a default value with unwrap_or makes invalid input look successful. map_err converts a ParseIntError into the domain error while keeping the ? operator.

sections.title: Unit tests and integration tests
sections.body: Tests inside a module can reach private items. Files under tests/ compile as separate crates and can only use the public API, which makes them a good check that the exported surface is usable. Cargo builds and runs both when you run cargo test.

sections.title: Features determine what compiles
sections.body: Code behind #[cfg(feature = "cli")] is removed from the crate when the feature is off. A default cargo test run never sees those tests. CI should run cargo test --all-features or a matrix that covers each feature.

quiz.prompt: The quantity tests are inside #[cfg(all(test, feature = "cli"))], and CI runs cargo test with default features. What does CI miss?

options.label: The gated tests are not compiled; run cargo test --all-features or a feature matrix.
Nothing; cargo test always compiles every feature.
Only the integration tests; unit tests always run.
The lockfile update, which is unrelated to features.

quiz.explanation: cfg(feature = "cli") removes the test module when the feature is off. A default cargo test run never compiles or executes it. CI must enable the feature or cover each feature in a matrix.

accessibility.summary: The workspace is keyboard accessible. Checks verify source structure and the reference tests; they do not compile or run the framework.
accessibility.keyboardNotes: Use Tab to move between the editor and results. Ctrl+Enter runs the checks.
accessibility.screenReaderNotes: Each check announces its description, whether it passed, and the missing or forbidden source fragment or test failure.
